q1_issues.issue: "right behind Melissa" answers *where*, which the oblique rule routes to the named role Location; the preposition-named (Behind ...) form is licensed only when no named role fits, and the instruction set says to decide by the question the PP answers.

q2_gaps: relative spatial position PPs ("behind / in front of / next to X") - every where-answering PP is routed to Location, so a clause carrying both a containing place ("in class") and a relative position ("behind Melissa") has no way to keep the two distinct
degree modifier on a spatial preposition ("right behind", "just behind") - Degree is defined only for adjectives and for quantities, so the intensifier "right" has nowhere to go and was dropped
notes: Experiencer on the postural stative "sat" matches the intransitive-subject rule and its own "the crate sat in the bay" example; both Names, Past, and the bare-NP constant `class` for "in class" are all correct. The Behind/Location tension is arguably forced by the gap above rather than by carelessness.
